QF.id: Terminology in Equity and Debt Markets_11

question.text: The approximate Yield to Maturity (YTM) formula is:

explanation.text: The Logic: The approximate YTM (sometimes called the bond-equivalent or "ad-hoc" YTM) blends the annual coupon income with the annualised capital gain or loss the investor will realise by holding the bond to maturity. The standard approximation is [Coupon + (Face Value - Price)/n] / [(Face Value + Price)/2], where n is the number of years to maturity. The numerator represents annual income (coupon plus pro-rated discount/premium to par), and the denominator represents the average of face value and price as a proxy for invested capital. The Trap: Coupon / Face Value gives the coupon rate, not yield to maturity. Market Price / EPS is the price-to-earnings ratio, an equity metric. Dividend / Market Price is the dividend yield, also an equity metric. None of these account for the capital gain/loss component embedded in a bond bought above or below par. Note: The cited NISM Series XV Research Analyst workbook pages checked (pp.67-68) define YTM conceptually and indicate it can be solved by trial-and-error or XIRR, but do not state the closed-form approximation formula above. The formula reflects general industry/regulatory teaching of YTM rather than the cited workbook chapter.
